extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PIs, postdocs, K/R applicants) seeking practical funding and resubmission advice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, mechanism-specific guidance and evaluative criteria for preparing, resubmitting, and tracking NIH extramural grant applications (K/K99/K25, R01, R03, R15, R21, DP2, P01, etc.), and for communicating with Program Officers and Grants Management Specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary IC assignment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not have a secondary IC assigned, it is too late to add one – end of story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment of secondary ICs must be in place before review/processing; you cannot add a secondary IC after assignment or after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether secondary IC will fund an application
rubrics_metrics.description: Many ICs do not fund secondary assignments (eg, NIGMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do have a secondary IC assigned, contact the PO at that IC to see whether their IC would consider picking up your application. If the secondary IC is interested, the original IC must formally relinquish the application and the secondary PO must indicate interest; relinquishment may be delayed until end of fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer (PO) as source of resubmission advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask your PO whether you should resubmit; ask whether the PO would like you to write a brief rebuttal to the summary statement (Summary of Discussion section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before preparing a resubmission, contact the PO (ideally after summary statement release) to ask whether to resubmit and to get guidance on addressing key weaknesses; have a list of topics/questions prepared for the conversation because time is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't mention prior A1 score in new A0
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time you submit a new A0 after a prior A1, you do not mention the prior review or its score or refer to the last submitted application in any way in the new A0 application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any FOA and mechanism, an A0 following a previous A1 must not reference or discuss the prior submission's review or score.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT request indicates active consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If you were asked to submit JIT, this means the IC is considering your application for a possible award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JIT (Just-in-Time) requests and eRA Commons statuses like 'Pending administrative review' are positive signs (not guarantees) that the application is being processed for award. After JIT submission, the Grants Management Specialist (GMS) handles administrative processing; POs are typically out of the loop for timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons status meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Status changes such as 'Pending administrative review' or 'Award prepared' are indicators of processing stage and often a good sign of impending award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor eRA Commons for status updates; contact the GMS (not the PO) for timing estimates if you need to plan pre-award spending, but avoid unnecessary inquiries that may slow processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC paylines and timing (interim vs final)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs will not have their final paylines until after the federal budget is signed into law; ICs receive appropriations about 6-8 weeks after the federal budget, and final paylines are retroactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim paylines may be posted earlier; final paylines can change after budget passage. POs often cannot give definitive funding likelihood until IC appropriations are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC-specific funding flexibility (beyond score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs (e.g., GM) have flexibility to look beyond score when making funding decisions and are not strictly payline-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different ICs have different policies: GM may consider other programmatic factors; other ICs rarely fund applications where they are listed as secondary. Ask the PO for IC-specific behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role separation: PO vs GMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Your PO is not involved in grant processing (NOA timing, administrative actions); GMS handles administrative processing and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the GMS for administrative timeline estimates or pre-award account questions; POs advise on science/program fit and resubmission strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for Council and resubmission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait until Council meets to hear IC advice on whether to resubmit; you can be preparing a resubmission in the meantime (draft responses/introduction) as insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO is unresponsive and Council timing is imminent, draft a response to prior review and prepare an A1 for the next submission cycle so you can submit quickly if advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to conduct a Program Officer conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: When you talk with a PO, have a list of topics, points, and/or questions written down; ask whether you should plan to resubmit and address key weaknesses raised in the Summary of Discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask PO what reviewers want to see, whether a brief rebuttal would help, when to check back, and whether to begin preparing a resubmission; PO can advise on target SRG/IC fit based on their recollection of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a rebuttal/Introduction for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft a response to prior review (e.g., Introduction) addressing primary weaknesses raised in the Summary of Discussion to be ready if resubmission is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, concise response to critiques helps POs and reviewers evaluate the changes; prepare it while awaiting PO/Council decisions to save time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing SRG/study section and matching tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask the PO for the best study section to target; use Matchmaker (RePORTER) and ART (CSR) with your Specific Aims to search SRGs and past awards to identify appropriate reviewers/panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping your aims and searching SRG histories helps you target a panel where similar science has scored well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications to same SRG
rubrics_metrics.description: Having two applications at the same SRG will not affect your review—reviewers consider the scientific merit of each application individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs (not SRGs) decide funding and may prefer portfolio spread; make sure POs view multiple applications as distinct and high priority to avoid thematic overlap concerns during funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award/eligibility interactions across mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If an R01 is funded first, you would no longer be eligible for certain ESI-restricted mechanisms (e.g., Trailblazer R21) and that application would be administratively withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions can change eligibility for other pending applications; you cannot convert an application administratively to a different FOA because of a loss of eligibility—resubmission to the appropriate FOA would be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on simultaneous applications/awards
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot have the same application under review at the same time and cannot accept two awards for the same research; you can only hold one R15 award concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have related pending applications, discuss strategy with your PO to avoid duplicate funding or eligibility conflicts; JIT and award processes check for overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget increase expectations for renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for any amount under $500k; most Institutes limit increases to 3%-20% (varies by IC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with your PO on what is reasonable for a renewal budget at your IC before preparing the detailed budget; above $500k requires permission to submit in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC-specific administrative budget policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs disallow inflationary/inflationary salary increases (example: NIH disallowed inflationary increases in FY12 & FY13; AHRQ has formal policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm IC policy on salary/cola and allowable budget changes with PO or FOA guidance when preparing JIT or renewal budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: P01 PI and project PI experience expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although there is no strict requirement, P01 PI and project PIs are expected to have R01 experience; all project PIs should also be R01 awardees, though they can be paired with a junior PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the PO for a pre-application meeting to present program theme and project design and to get candid advice on PI competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 PI eligibility constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: The R15 PI-eligibility website says 'The PI may not be the PI of an active NIH research grant at the time of an R15 award'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold an active NIH research grant, check with the R15 PO before applying or investing effort in an R15 submission; acceptance of another award may require choosing between awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing IC on resubmission and SEP considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: You can absolutely change ICs when resubmitting; if reviewed in a Special Emphasis Panel (SEP), ask the new IC PO whether you will be reviewed in the same SEP or a different panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the resubmission will be reviewed by a different panel, consult the PO about whether submitting as an A0 or A1 is preferable and tailor the application to the new IC's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC assignment is based on science; how to request a change
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment is based on the science you propose in your application. You can suggest an IC but you don’t get to pick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you prefer another IC, talk to the assigned IC PO and the PO at the requested IC to explain fit and seek agreement; you must convince both that the proposal better fits the requested IC's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO responsiveness and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: POs may delay definitive answers due to budget/continuing resolution timing; if a PO does not reply, copy the Branch Chief to ensure someone provides resubmission advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document communications, be polite, and use chain-of-command if needed; prepare resubmission materials in parallel if advice is delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading FOA and pre-application preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Announcement/FOA carefully; follow FOA-specific instructions (e.g., Katz R01: 'Do NOT include any preliminary data', ensure your research fits the listed IC missions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talk to a PO early, follow FOA rules exactly, be skeptical of informal advice, and tailor submissions to the FOA's stated requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting 'remains under consideration' vs 'not selected in first round'
rubrics_metrics.description: If PO says 'not selected in the first round but remains under consideration', it typically means your application may be on a list for later funding decisions, pending budget clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect possible delays (months) during continuing resolutions or until the IC has budget clarity; ask PO whether to prepare a resubmission in the interim.
